headline.scope: normal built-in-speaker use; controlled mid/high band is much tighter than deep-bass household-mic uncertainty

controlled_two_pass_consumer_matrix.method: same-run physical fundamental / digital fundamental; two full passes; common rows require <=1 dB repeat consistency; household impulses therefore fail or are excluded

environmental_confidence.note: The SP7 fixture is in a normal household, not an anechoic chamber. Repeat gating and coherent tone extraction are treated as stronger evidence than raw broadband RMS.

controlled_two_pass_consumer_matrix.historical_correction: The 2026-08-18 Windows-only ~+7.7 dB median 0.05->0.20 expansion observation does not reproduce on current Windows under the current matched two-pass/repeat-gated acquisition. Treat it as historical state/acquisition-specific, not a stable Windows target.

seven_nation_army_program_material.source: The White Stripes - Seven Nation Army (Official Music Video).mp3

digital_band_parity_80_hz_to_10_khz.note: Windows loopback and Linux post-Dolby hardware-sink monitor were aligned to the same decoded MP3 excerpt.

noise_robust_physical_to_digital_transfe.method: multi-band source fingerprint alignment; 1 s band energies; trim top/bottom 10 percent of windows to suppress household impulses; compare physical/digital transfer per OS

seven_nation_army_program_material.environment_note: The Windows music take had materially lower fingerprint confidence than the Linux take, consistent with household acoustic contamination. Deep-bass residuals are therefore lower-confidence than 315 Hz+ results and are not used to justify a PA/EQ change.

decision.reason: Current PA24 Golden v32 already overlays current Windows within a few tenths of a dB over the controlled/useful band. Raising PA gain would change a working variable without evidence that it improves parity.
decision.remaining_acoustic_work: Repeat deep-bass measurements when the room is quiet and/or with a more controlled acoustic fixture if a sub-315-Hz parity claim is desired.
